attempts.summary: Created a locked-password 'opsbot' account on both node1 and node2 (RHEL 7.9), generated an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installed the public key into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and confirmed opsbot@node1 can SSH into opsbot@node2 non-interactively. Discovered and fixed an sshd_config quirk on both nodes where an earlier 'PasswordAuthentication yes' directive (line 65) silently shadowed a later 'no' (OpenSSH honors the first occurrence of a keyword), so password auth was still effectively enabled; corrected the first occurrence to 'no' on both nodes, validated with 'sshd -t' and 'sshd -T', and reloaded sshd. Verified password authentication is rejected for opsbot on both nodes (server only offers publickey/gssapi) while key-based access continues to work. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured baseline boot_id/uptime and service health, rebooted node1 then node2 sequentially, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd health, opsbot account/lock state, key files, and the opsbot@node1 -> opsbot@node2 SSH flow after each restart.
